items.stem: Why is the initial margin on a futures contract best described as a performance bond rather than a purchase price?

options.text: It is a good-faith deposit securing the position, not the full contract value
options.rationale: Correct: futures margin is a performance bond; daily settlement adjusts it, unlike paying full value.

options.text: It is a loan from the broker charged at interest
options.rationale: Unlike equity margin, futures margin is a deposit, not a borrowed sum.

options.text: It is the total amount the trader can ever lose
options.rationale: Losses can exceed the initial margin through daily settlement.

options.text: It is a fee kept by the exchange
options.rationale: Margin is a returnable deposit, not a fee.

items.explanation: Correct: futures margin is a performance bond; daily settlement adjusts it, unlike paying full value.

items.stem: Which TWO statements describe a commodity futures curve in contango? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Longer-dated contracts trade at higher prices than nearer-dated ones
options.rationale: Correct: an upward-sloping curve with later months higher is contango.

options.text: A holder rolling a long position may face a cost as the curve converges
options.rationale: Correct: rolling up the curve in contango can create a negative roll yield.

options.text: Nearer-dated contracts always cost more than later ones
options.rationale: That describes backwardation, the opposite of contango.

options.text: Contango means the market expects immediate shortage
options.rationale: An expected near-term shortage typically produces backwardation, not contango.

items.explanation: Correct: an upward-sloping curve with later months higher is contango.

items.stem: A speculator holds a long crude-oil future that is nearing expiry and does not want delivery. What should they do?

options.text: Close or roll the position to a later contract before expiry
options.rationale: Correct: closing or rolling avoids obligations tied to holding a physically settled contract into delivery.

options.text: Hold it to expiry to avoid transaction costs
options.rationale: Holding a physically settled contract to expiry can trigger delivery obligations.

options.text: Convert the contract into shares of the oil company
options.rationale: A futures contract cannot be converted into equity shares.
Ignoring expiry is exactly what creates delivery risk.

items.explanation: Correct: closing or rolling avoids obligations tied to holding a physically settled contract into delivery.
